title: Employee Incentive
description: Monthly incentive earned by every incentivised role — Technician, Team Lead, Service Advisor, Job Controller, Quality Controller, Bodyshop Estimator and Insurance BD — with the payout broken down by the component that earned it and the achievement figure behind each one, at parity with the Employee Incentive Calculation report.
notes:
Mirrors pitstop_email_digest's Employee Incentive Calculation report. One row per employee per calendar month per role, with the ladder already applied to that month's totals, so the amounts sum across months and roles but the percentages do not — read a percentage for a single month, never as a total.

The grain is the calendar month because an incentive is a monthly award: the ladders score a whole period's totals, and the revenue targets are read from the monthly columns of Target Role. The query covers a rolling twelve months.

Ladders, weightages and base incentives are transcribed into SQL CASE expressions from the util_<designation> modules and the DEFAULT_INCENTIVE_AMT_MAP in employee_incentive_calculation.js (Technician 350, Team Lead 600, Service Advisor 700, Job Controller 500, Quality Controller 450, Bodyshop Estimator 600, Insurance BD 1750). They are a copy, not a reference: changing a rate in the Python or the JS does NOT change this dashboard, and both must be edited together.

WIP ageing is scored against the configured wip_ageing_ladder — under 46 days pays for the Service Advisor, under 45 for the Job Controller. This matches the report as of the fix to apply_wip_ageing in util_employee_incentive_calculation.py, which previously carried a for/else bug that paid the WIP weightage in full to every Service Advisor and Job Controller regardless of age, and scored both roles against a hardcoded 46.0 instead of their own ladders. A copy of this dashboard taken before that fix will read lower than the report it was built from.

One deliberate difference remains, and it is the same one the Workshop Turnover template makes: a timesheet line is attributed to the month it STARTS in rather than split across the months it overlaps, so a shift running through midnight on the 1st lands wholly in the earlier month. The effect is a fraction of a percent on the Technician and Job Controller totals and nothing at all on the other roles.

WIP ageing for a past month is approximate: open-ness is read from the project's CURRENT status, so a project closed since is missing from the months when it was still open. Only the current month's WIP figure is exact. Everything else is reconstructed from dated records and is exact for any month.

Identity differs by role, because the report's own grouping does. Technician, Quality Controller, Bodyshop Estimator and Insurance BD rows are keyed by Employee; Team Lead rows by the Task's reporting manager and Job Controller rows by the Task's job controller (both Employees); Service Advisor rows by Sales Person, which is what Project.service_advisor links to. The employee_id column therefore holds a Sales Person for Service Advisor rows and an Employee everywhere else.

Available hours come from submitted Present/Half Day Attendance, capped at today, falling back to the standard hours for a present-but-unclocked today — the same rule the Workshop Productivity report applies. The report distributes each attendance key's hours across its rows and re-aggregates them; because every role's grouping field is itself part of that key, the distribution cancels and this query sums them directly, which is exact rather than approximate.

Two report behaviours reproduced as-is, worth knowing when reading the numbers. Bodyshop Estimator and Insurance BD sales join Quotation to Project to Sales Invoice, so an invoice is counted once per quotation the estimator raised against that repair order — a second quotation double-counts it. And the Quality Controller feedback query filters on the literal designation 'Quality Controller' rather than on the designations configured in Incentive Calculation Setttings, so a differently-named QC designation scores no feedback.

Roles whose designations are unconfigured in Incentive Calculation Setttings behave as the report does: Quality Controller, Bodyshop Estimator and Insurance BD produce no rows at all, while Service Advisor falls back to every service advisor with invoiced sales.
